sentences.en: Today, a two-part update on the pandemic with my colleagues, Carl Zimmer and Abby Goodnoff.

sentences.en: It's Monday, January 11th.
sentences.zh: 今天是1月11日，星期一。

sentences.en: Good afternoon, everybody, and thank you for joining the latest coronavirus press conference.
sentences.zh: 大家下午好，感谢参加最新的一次新冠疫情新闻发布会。

sentences.en: It seems that the spread is now being driven by the new variant of the virus.
sentences.zh: 目前疫情的蔓延似乎是由这种病毒的新变种驱动的。

sentences.en: Cases in London and the southeast of England are skyrocketing.
sentences.zh: 伦敦和英格兰东南部的病例正在激增。

sentences.en: The new variant is out of control, and we need to bring it under control.
sentences.zh: 这种新变种已经失控，我们需要将其控制住。

sentences.en: And it's been detected in at least 17 other countries.
sentences.zh: 而且它已经在至少其他17个国家被检测到。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, we now know this U.K.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，我们现在知道这种英国

sentences.en: variant is in Colorado.
sentences.zh: 变种已经出现在科罗拉多州。

sentences.en: It's in California.
sentences.zh: 它出现在加利福尼亚州。

sentences.en: A man in the state of New York has now tested positive for COVID-19 with that same U.K.
sentences.zh: 纽约州的一名男子新冠病毒检测呈阳性，感染的正是这种英国

sentences.en: variant.
sentences.zh: 变种。

sentences.en: The U.K.
sentences.zh: 这种英国

sentences.en: strain could be a game-changer.
sentences.zh: 毒株可能会改变游戏规则。

sentences.en: Carl, where does the story of this British variant of the coronavirus start?
sentences.zh: 卡尔，这种英国新冠病毒变种的故事是从哪里开始的？

sentences.en: The story starts around the beginning of December, and actually in South Africa.
sentences.zh: 故事始于12月初，实际上是在南非。

sentences.en: There, scientists notice that there's a variant of the coronavirus that is spreading around very quickly, and it has them very worried.
sentences.zh: 在那里，科学家们注意到有一种新冠病毒变种正在迅速传播，这让他们非常担心。

sentences.en: And so scientists in the United Kingdom take a look at those mutations in the virus, and they say, hmm, I wonder if any of our viruses have any of those mutations.
sentences.zh: 于是，英国的科学家们研究了病毒的这些突变，他们想，嗯，不知道我们的病毒是否也有这些突变。

sentences.en: And lo and behold, they find one lineage of viruses that has some of these mutations and a bunch of others.
sentences.zh: 结果发现，他们确实找到了一个病毒谱系，它不仅具有其中一些突变，还带有其他许多突变。

sentences.en: And they get really worried about it because the more they look at it, the more they realize this variant is spreading like crazy throughout England.
sentences.zh: 他们对此感到非常担忧，因为研究得越深入，他们就越意识到这种变种正在整个英格兰疯狂传播。

sentences.en: And once they make that announcement, scientists in other countries say, hey, oh, what if we have that too?
sentences.zh: 一旦他们发布了这个公告，其他国家的科学家就说，嘿，哦，如果我们也有这种情况怎么办？

sentences.en: And so by the end of December, in the United States, scientists are starting to find rare cases of this variant in states across the country, from California now all the way to
sentences.zh: 因此，到了12月底，在美国，科学家们开始在全国各地的州发现这种变种的零星病例，从加利福尼亚州一直到

sentences.en: New York.
sentences.zh: 纽约州。

sentences.en: So it's been here for a while.
sentences.zh: 所以它已经存在一段时间了。

sentences.en: We don't know how long.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道具体有多久。

sentences.en: But our country has already been seeded with this variant.
sentences.zh: 但我们的国家已经被这种变种播下了种子。

sentences.en: And what exactly is the mutation?
sentences.zh: 那么这种突变到底是什么？

sentences.en: What makes it different from the coronavirus that we have all come to know?
sentences.zh: 是什么让它与我们所熟知的新冠病毒不同？

sentences.en: Well, scientists right now only have some ideas.
sentences.zh: 嗯，科学家们目前只有一些想法。

sentences.en: Right now, there are actually experiments going on in laboratories testing out this variant to see what it is that makes it biologically special.
sentences.zh: 目前，实验室里确实正在进行实验，测试这种变种，看看是什么让它在生物学上变得特别。

sentences.en: So we don't know for sure.
sentences.zh: 所以我们还不确定。

sentences.en: But there's an idea that when you breathe in these viruses, they are stickier.
sentences.zh: 但有一种观点认为，当你吸入这些病毒时，它们更具粘性。

sentences.en: So the coronavirus is covered with these flower-like proteins called spike.
sentences.zh: 新冠病毒表面覆盖着这些花状的蛋白质，称为刺突蛋白。

sentences.en: And when it's floating around in your airway, these spike proteins can latch on to certain proteins on the surface of our own cells.
sentences.zh: 当它在你的呼吸道中漂浮时，这些刺突蛋白可以附着在我们细胞表面的特定蛋白质上。

sentences.en: And if they can get a tight grip, then they can basically pull themselves inside of our cells.
sentences.zh: 如果它们能紧紧抓住，基本上就能把自己拉进我们的细胞里。

sentences.en: And there they can replicate.
sentences.zh: 然后它们就可以在那里进行复制。

sentences.en: So if you want to be successful as a coronavirus, you want to have a good spike protein that gets you into the cells of your hoSt.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你想成为一种成功的新冠病毒，你需要有一个好的刺突蛋白，让你进入宿主的细胞。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Now, scientists suspect that maybe some of these mutations are giving it that improvement.
sentences.zh: 现在，科学家们怀疑可能正是其中一些突变赋予了它这种改进。

sentences.en: In other words, the spike protein is grabbing on tighter onto our cells and giving that virus a better shot at making copies of itself.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，刺突蛋白抓得更紧了，从而让病毒有更好的机会进行自我复制。

sentences.en: So just how much more effective is this mutated variant coronavirus at infecting people?
sentences.zh: 那么这种突变后的新冠病毒在感染人方面到底有多有效？

sentences.en: Is it measurable?
sentences.zh: 这是可以衡量的吗？

sentences.en: It is measurable.
sentences.zh: 是可以衡量的。

sentences.en: And the difference is big.
sentences.zh: 而且差异很大。

sentences.en: The way that epidemiologists talk about this is something called R-naught, or the reproductive number.
sentences.zh: 流行病学家谈论这个问题时使用了一个术语，叫R0，即基本传染数。

sentences.en: And what that means basically is in a given situation, on average, how many people does an infected person infect?
sentences.zh: 简单来说，它的意思是，在特定情况下，平均而言，一个感染者会传染给多少人？

sentences.en: So if you have an R-naught of one, that means each person who's infected, on average, just infects one more person.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你的R0是1，这意味着每个感染者平均只会再传染给一个人。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Now, scientists in England took a look at how this new variant did during a November lockdown compared to the other variants.
sentences.zh: 现在，英国的科学家们观察了这种新变种在11月封锁期间与其他变种相比的表现。

sentences.en: With the other variants, the lockdown was fairly effective.
sentences.zh: 对于其他变种，封锁相当有效。

sentences.en: They estimate that the R-naught was 0.95.
sentences.zh: 他们估计R0为0.95。

sentences.en: So it's under one, which is good.
sentences.zh: 所以它低于1，这是好事。

sentences.en: But the new variant, under the same conditions, had an R-naught of 1.45.
sentences.zh: 但在相同条件下，新变种的R0为1.45。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 哦，哇。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That's a lot higher.
sentences.zh: 这高出很多。

sentences.en: And that can make a big difference in terms of fueling an explosive growth in your outbreak, which, unfortunately, is exactly what is happening in the United Kingdom right now.
sentences.zh: 这可能会在助长疫情爆发式增长方面产生巨大差异，不幸的是，这正是英国目前正在发生的情况。

sentences.en: And this new variant now has, in the past few months, essentially taken over the country.
sentences.zh: 在过去的几个月里，这种新变种基本上已经接管了整个国家。

sentences.en: So doing a little bit of math here, 0.9 to 1.4, that's about a 50% increase, which is very significant.
sentences.zh: 所以简单算一下，从0.9到1.4，大约增加了50%，这非常显著。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's about 50% better at getting from one person to another.
sentences.zh: 它在人与人之间传播的能力提高了大约50%。

sentences.en: And just how scary is that, for those of us who don't think about R-naughts and the math of transmission?
sentences.zh: 对于我们这些不考虑R0和传播数学的人来说，这有多可怕？

sentences.en: Wouldn't that seem to suggest that going about our lives the way we currently are, even with a mask on, having the kind of interactions that we are currently having, that might be
sentences.zh: 这难道不是在暗示，如果我们继续像现在这样生活，即使戴着口罩，进行我们目前正在进行的互动，那可能

sentences.en: 50% riskier?
sentences.zh: 风险会增加50%吗？

sentences.en: Yes, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So given that, I'm curious how behaviors are now supposed to change.
sentences.zh: 既然如此，我很好奇行为现在应该如何改变。

sentences.en: Does six feet apart change to 10 feet apart, 12 feet apart, or what?
sentences.zh: 六英尺的距离要变成10英尺、12英尺，还是怎样？

sentences.en: I think maybe six feet apart changes to just stay at home.
sentences.zh: 我想也许六英尺的距离应该变成直接待在家里。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Because anything you do that puts you at risk of an infection has now got a bigger risk.
sentences.zh: 因为你所做的任何让你面临感染风险的事情，现在的风险都更大了。

sentences.en: So if you go to the grocery store and maybe there was a 10% risk you had of breathing in a virus from an infected person in the line behind you, now that's a 15% risk.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你去杂货店，也许你排在你身后感染者呼吸出的病毒的风险是10%，现在变成了15%。

sentences.en: If you just repeat that over and over and over again, from person to person to person, you start to have a huge difference.
sentences.zh: 如果你只是不断地重复这个过程，从一个人传给另一个人，你就会开始看到巨大的差异。

sentences.en: And ordinary measures that we're taking that we think are really effective lockdown measures may not be enough.
sentences.zh: 我们正在采取的、我们认为非常有效的封锁措施可能还不够。

sentences.en: We may have to look for more drastic measures to slow this thing down.
sentences.zh: 我们可能需要寻找更严厉的措施来减缓这种病毒的传播。

sentences.en: And Carl, drastic as in what?
sentences.zh: 卡尔，严厉是指什么？

sentences.en: Well, for example, every American could be supplied with a high quality mask and then be required to wear it outside.
sentences.zh: 嗯，例如，可以给每个美国人提供高质量的口罩，并要求他们在户外佩戴。

sentences.en: We could have massive testing, for example, at-home tests that people take every single day.
sentences.zh: 我们可以进行大规模检测，例如人们每天都可以进行的居家测试。

sentences.en: We could do these sorts of things and really be much more aggressive at stopping this virus.
sentences.zh: 我们可以做这些事情，并在阻止这种病毒方面采取更积极的态度。

sentences.en: And we're going to need to be more aggressive because this virus is just better at getting around.
sentences.zh: 我们需要更积极，因为这种病毒在传播方面就是更厉害。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Carl, in our conversations with colleagues, including Donald G.
sentences.zh: 卡尔，在我们与包括小唐纳德·G·麦克尼尔在内的同事的谈话中，我们被告知新冠病毒的突变往往会随着时间的推移变得不那么危险，而不是更危险，毒性降低，而不是增强。

sentences.en: McNeil Jr., we have been told that mutations in the coronavirus tend to make it less dangerous over time, not more dangerous, less lethal, not more lethal.
sentences.zh: 这里的情况是这样吗？

sentences.en: Is that the case here?
sentences.zh: 这种情况有时会发生在某些病毒身上。

sentences.en: That does happen sometimes with some viruses.
sentences.zh: 但并非所有病毒都是如此。

sentences.en: It doesn't happen with all of them.
sentences.zh: 而且肯定不会立即发生。

sentences.en: And it certainly doesn't happen right away.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，没有证据表明感染这种变种会更安全。

sentences.en: And in this case, there's no evidence that this variant is any safer to get.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们还发现，如果你感染了这种变种，它并不比感染其他新冠变种更危险。

sentences.en: Now, what we also are finding is that it's not any more dangerous if you get this than if you get another variant of COVID.
sentences.zh: 你最终住院的风险是一样的。

sentences.en: You still have the same kind of risk of ending up in the hospital.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，因为它似乎传染性极强，这意味着总体上会有更多的人住院。

sentences.en: The problem is that because this seems to be so contagious, it means that overall, a lot more people are going to go into the hospital.
sentences.zh: 这也意味着会有更多的人死亡。

sentences.en: And it also means a lot more people are going to die.
sentences.zh: 我们已经在英国看到，医院正被新冠患者淹没，其中许多人感染了这种新变种。

sentences.en: We're already seeing in the United Kingdom, hospitals are being overwhelmed with COVID patients, many of whom have this new variant.
sentences.zh: 所以这可能不是什么可怕的超级杀手变种，但我们必须极其认真地对待它。

sentences.en: So this may not be some terrible, super killer variant, but it's one that we have to take incredibly seriously.
sentences.zh: 那么卡尔，目前英国变种在美国的传播范围有多广？

sentences.en: So Carl, at this point, just how widespread is the British variant within the United States?
sentences.zh: 我们真的不知道。

sentences.en: We don't really know.
sentences.zh: 我们在八个州发现了它。

sentences.en: We have found it in eight states.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止有62例，但我们实际上并没有进行那种真正能看清情况所需的检测。

sentences.en: There have been 62 cases so far, but we're not actually doing the kinds of tests that you need to do to really get a good look at what's going on.
sentences.zh: 我们只是在这里或那里偶然发现了这种变种。

sentences.en: We're just sort of stumbling across the variant here and there.
sentences.zh: 美国基本上是在盲目飞行。

sentences.en: The United States is really basically flying blind.
sentences.zh: 为什么会这样，卡尔？

sentences.en: And why is that, Carl?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们不做必要的检测来告诉我们这种变种的传播范围有多广？

sentences.en: Why are we not doing the testing required to tell us how widespread the variant is?
sentences.zh: 这感觉是我们大家都非常想知道的事情。

sentences.en: That feels like something we all definitely want to know.
sentences.zh: 这确实是我们想知道的事情，也是我们需要知道的事情。

sentences.en: It is something we want to know, and it's something we need to know.
sentences.zh: 但美国并没有投资于我们需要的那种组织工作来完成它。

sentences.en: But the United States has not invested in the kind of organization we need to do it.
sentences.zh: 我们可以以英国为例，看看如何正确地做这件事。

sentences.en: We can look to the United Kingdom as an example of how to do it right.
sentences.zh: 3月份，他们建立了一个完整的项目，大规模收集病毒，并

sentences.en: In March, they set up a whole program to actually collect viruses on a massive scale and actually
sentences.zh: 观察它们所有的遗传物质，查看数十万种病毒的所谓基因组。

sentences.en: look at all of their genetic material, looking at what are called genomes of hundreds of thousands of viruses.
sentences.zh: 我们只是以一种非常杂乱无章的方式观察其中极小极小的一部分。

sentences.en: We're looking at a tiny, tiny fraction of that in a very disorganized fashion.
sentences.zh: 有些州做得相当不错。

sentences.en: Some states are doing a pretty good job.
sentences.zh: 有些州根本没有对任何基因组进行测序。

sentences.en: Some states haven't sequenced any genomes at all.
sentences.zh: 这很混乱。

sentences.en: It's disorganized.
sentences.zh: 目前几乎没有国家层面的领导，这就是我们所处的境地。

sentences.en: There is very little national leadership at this point, and this is what we're left with.
sentences.zh: 那么卡尔，考虑到所有这些，特别是关于我们盲目飞行这一令人沮丧的消息，我认为这自然会引出疫苗问题。

sentences.en: So, Carl, given all of that, especially this depressing news of just how blindly we are flying, I think this naturally brings us to vaccines.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，英国和美国批准的辉瑞和莫德纳疫苗，对这种新变种的有效性是否与原始版本一样？

sentences.en: Are the vaccines that have been approved in both the United Kingdom and the United States so far, from Pfizer, from Moderna, are they as effective against this new variant of the
sentences.zh: 嗯，要得到确切的答案，你必须进行实验。

sentences.en: virus as the original version of it?
sentences.zh: 实际上已经发布了一个实验，结果证明

sentences.en: Well, to get a definitive answer to that, you have to do experiments.
sentences.zh: 辉瑞公司生产的疫苗对这种新变种中的一个关键突变绝对有效，这是人们一直非常担心的突变。

sentences.en: And there has actually been one experiment so far that's been released, and it turns out that the
sentences.zh: 看起来没问题。

sentences.en: vaccine made by Pfizer is definitely effective against one of the key mutations in this new variant, one that people have been really worried about.
sentences.zh: 现在，还有其他突变是科学家们需要研究的，在我们真正感到完全脱离危险之前。

sentences.en: And it seems fine.
sentences.zh: 但我确实认为，根据我们目前所知，我们可以对这些疫苗充满信心。

sentences.en: Now, there are other mutations that scientists are going to have to look at as well before we can really feel like we're totally out of the woods.
sentences.zh: 所以真正重要的是，我们要尽快让尽可能多的人接种这种疫苗。

sentences.en: But I do think that we can be confident in these vaccines from what we know so far.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so what's really important is that we get this vaccine as quickly as possible into as many people as possible.
sentences.zh: 这似乎给疫苗的推广增加了极大的紧迫性。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: This would seem to add extraordinary urgency to the rollout of the vaccine.
sentences.zh: 我们必须让人们接种疫苗。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 我们仍然必须保持这些社交距离措施。

sentences.en: We've got to get people vaccinated.
sentences.zh: 我们必须走在病毒前面，否则它真的会给我们造成很大的伤害。

sentences.en: We have to still keep up these social distancing measures.
sentences.zh: 好的，卡尔，非常感谢。

sentences.en: We've got to get ahead of this thing, because otherwise it's going to really do us a lot of damage.
sentences.zh: 我们很感激。

sentences.en: Well, Carl, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app unlocked.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序已解锁。

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to The Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道，你需要订阅《纽约时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore The Times for a month for free without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果能免费试用《纽约时报》一个月，且无需绑定信用卡，你愿意吗？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在机会来了。

sentences.en: When you download The New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 首次下载《纽约时报》应用程序，即可免费使用一个月。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 这一个月，你可以突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么内容。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to The New York Times, download The Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载应用程序，获取30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: So, Abby, we just spoke to our colleague, Carl Zimmer, about the dangers of the British variant
sentences.zh: 艾比，我们刚刚和同事卡尔·齐默谈过，讨论了英国变异新冠病毒的危险性，

sentences.en: of the coronavirus and the pressure it is putting on everyone to vaccinate as quickly as possible.
sentences.zh: 以及它给所有人带来的尽快接种疫苗的压力。

sentences.en: And you have been tracking vaccinations in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 你一直在追踪美国的疫苗接种情况。

sentences.en: And I recall that the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我记得美国

sentences.en: government said that it wanted to vaccinate 20 million Americans by the end of December.
sentences.zh: 政府曾表示，希望在12月底前为2000万美国人接种疫苗。

sentences.en: But that did not happen.
sentences.zh: 但目标没有实现。

sentences.en: It is well into January.
sentences.zh: 现在已经是1月中旬了。

sentences.en: And the U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国

sentences.en: has distributed about 22 million doses.
sentences.zh: 已经分发了约2200万剂疫苗。

sentences.en: And of those 22 million doses, about 8 million have actually been injected into people's arMs.
sentences.zh: 而在那2200万剂中，只有约800万剂真正注射到了人们的胳膊上。

sentences.en: So fewer than half of the doses.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，不到一半的剂量被使用了。

sentences.en: So how do you account for that really significant gap, that failure to meet these goals, and what feels like a pretty sluggish start to U.S.
sentences.zh: 那么，你如何解释这种巨大的差距，即未能实现目标，以及美国疫苗接种工作

sentences.en: vaccinations?
sentences.zh: 看起来相当缓慢的开局？

sentences.en: Well, there's a million different reasons you could cite here.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你可以列举出一百万个原因。

sentences.en: And every state has its own reasons.
sentences.zh: 每个州都有自己的理由。

sentences.en: But there are some snowstorms, some bad weather, including a big snowstorm in the Northeast that bogged things down.
sentences.zh: 但确实有一些暴风雪和恶劣天气，包括东北部的一场大暴雪，拖慢了进度。

sentences.en: I've talked to a lot of people who have pointed to the holiday weeks really slowing things down.
sentences.zh: 我和很多人谈过，他们都指出假期周确实拖慢了进度。

sentences.en: Staff was low.
sentences.zh: 工作人员不足。

sentences.en: A lot of people were on vacation.
sentences.zh: 很多人在休假。

sentences.en: That seems to be a big thing.
sentences.zh: 这似乎是一个很大的因素。

sentences.en: And we'll find out in the next couple weeks if, in fact, things speed up.
sentences.zh: 我们会在接下来的几周内看看情况是否真的会加快。

sentences.en: And we can say, yes, the holidays were a big factor.
sentences.zh: 到时候我们就能说，是的，假期是一个重要因素。

sentences.en: You know, there's been some hesitancy and sometimes a lot of hesitancy among health care workers to get the vaccine, depending on where you are in the country.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在全国各地，医护人员对接种疫苗存在一些犹豫，有时甚至是非常犹豫，具体取决于你所在的地区。

sentences.en: So medical workers themselves are reluctant, in some cases, to take the vaccine.
sentences.zh: 所以，在某些情况下，医务人员自己也不愿接种疫苗。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Now, what I hear in talking to hospital people is generally doctors are taking the vaccine, and lots of nurses are taking the vaccine, super eager.
sentences.zh: 我从医院工作人员那里听到的情况是，医生们通常都在接种，很多护士也非常渴望接种。

sentences.en: But there's also a number of nurses who have not taken it, and a number of support workers in hospitals also refusing it.
sentences.zh: 但也有一些护士没有接种，还有一些医院的辅助人员也拒绝接种。

sentences.en: Nursing home staff refusing it, sometimes in large numbers.
sentences.zh: 养老院的工作人员拒绝接种，有时人数还不少。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: The governor of Ohio said the other day that something like 60% of nursing home staff in his state who have been offered the vaccine so far have turned it down.
sentences.zh: 俄亥俄州州长前几天说，在他所在的州，大约60%被提供疫苗的养老院员工拒绝了接种。

sentences.en: Huh.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So that kind of number really stops you and makes you wonder just how much this hesitancy is factoring into the sluggishness.
sentences.zh: 所以这个数字确实让人停下来思考，这种犹豫在多大程度上导致了进展缓慢。

sentences.en: But then we have other states like Massachusetts, where the governor said maybe 10% of nursing home staff have turned it down.
sentences.zh: 但我们也有像马萨诸塞州这样的州，州长说可能只有10%的养老院员工拒绝了接种。

sentences.en: Which is perhaps more along the lines of what we'd expect.
sentences.zh: 这可能更符合我们的预期。

sentences.en: So I think there's real variation depending on what part of the country we're in.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，根据我们所在的地区，情况确实存在很大差异。

sentences.en: Gotcha.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So the main takeaway when we think about why this has been slow is that there are more reasons than we can really keep track of at this point in the process.
sentences.zh: 所以当我们思考为什么进展缓慢时，主要的结论是，在目前的阶段，原因多到我们无法一一追踪。

sentences.en: There's a lot of reasons that are really hard to quantify.
sentences.zh: 有很多原因真的很难量化。

sentences.en: But one thing I'm noticing that's really interesting is this question that's emerging about how the CDC guidelines are affecting the speed of the rollout in different states.
sentences.zh: 但我注意到一个非常有趣的问题正在浮现，那就是疾控中心的指导方针如何影响了各州推广疫苗的速度。

sentences.en: Huh.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So describe this question, this debate.
sentences.zh: 描述一下这个问题，这场辩论。

sentences.en: So the CDC put out these guidelines last month on who should get vaccinated firSt.
sentences.zh: 疾控中心上个月发布了关于谁应该优先接种疫苗的指导方针。

sentences.en: You probably heard about them.
sentences.zh: 你可能听说过。

sentences.en: It starts with healthcare workers and nursing home residents and the staff who works in the nursing homes.
sentences.zh: 首先是医护人员、养老院居民以及在养老院工作的员工。

sentences.en: And they're not requirements.
sentences.zh: 这些不是强制要求。

sentences.en: They're not hard and fast rules that the states have to follow.
sentences.zh: 它们不是各州必须遵守的死板规则。

sentences.en: And so some people think following these guidelines really strictly is creating a bottleneck in the system.
sentences.zh: 因此，有些人认为严格遵循这些指导方针正在造成系统瓶颈。

sentences.en: Huh.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Especially when for whatever reason, many reasons, you don't have enough healthcare workers or nursing home residents to vaccinate on a given day or in a given week.
sentences.zh: 特别是当由于各种原因，你没有足够的医护人员或养老院居民在某一天或某一周内接种疫苗时。

sentences.en: And you get a lot of vaccines sitting around in the freezer.
sentences.zh: 你就会有很多疫苗闲置在冷冻柜里。

sentences.en: And, you know, the other camp says that those guidelines are there for a reason.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，另一派认为这些指导方针的存在是有原因的。

sentences.en: When you do have a very limited amount of vaccine, they're really good advice on who needs it moSt.
sentences.zh: 当你拥有的疫苗非常有限时，它们对于谁最需要疫苗是非常好的建议。

sentences.en: And also when you start allowing multiple groups to have access to the vaccine at once, it just creates a lot of chaos.
sentences.zh: 而且，当你开始允许多个群体同时获得疫苗时，只会造成很大的混乱。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And I have to imagine that different states are choosing to handle these federal guidelines very differently.
sentences.zh: 我不得不认为，不同的州在处理这些联邦指导方针时选择了截然不同的方式。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's up to each state how they distribute their supply of vaccine.
sentences.zh: 各州如何分配疫苗供应由他们自己决定。

sentences.en: And it's definitely all over the map.
sentences.zh: 而且情况确实千差万别。

sentences.en: And probably the two states that have represented the extremes of these two arguments are New
sentences.zh: 可能代表这两种观点极端的两个州是纽约州

sentences.en: York and Florida.
sentences.zh: 和佛罗里达州。

sentences.en: Good Monday morning.
sentences.zh: 周一早上好。

sentences.en: And tell me about New York firSt.
sentences.zh: 先跟我说说纽约州的情况。

sentences.en: How is it handling these guidelines?
sentences.zh: 它是如何处理这些指导方针的？

sentences.en: These vaccines are a valuable commodity.
sentences.zh: 这些疫苗是宝贵的商品。

sentences.en: Well, so initially, Governor Cuomo was sticking really strictly to the guidelines.
sentences.zh: 嗯，起初，科莫州长非常严格地遵守指导方针。

sentences.en: You're going to have some people who don't want to receive the vaccine.
sentences.zh: 总会有一些人不想接种疫苗。

sentences.en: I understand that.
sentences.zh: 我理解这一点。

sentences.en: But you're going to have a lot of people who want the vaccine desperately.
sentences.zh: 但也会有很多人非常渴望接种疫苗。

sentences.en: He talked about fining hospitals who gave shots to anyone who wasn't a frontline health care worker.
sentences.zh: 他曾谈到要对那些为非一线医护人员接种疫苗的医院进行罚款。

sentences.en: If there is fraudulent vaccination, that is very serious.
sentences.zh: 如果存在欺诈性接种，那是非常严重的。

sentences.en: That provider will lose their license, period.
sentences.zh: 该提供者将失去执照，没得商量。

sentences.en: He was really using strong language to warn against anyone daring to flout the state rules.
sentences.zh: 他确实用了严厉的措辞来警告任何敢于违抗州规则的人。

sentences.en: I don't care if you're a doctor, you're a nurse.
sentences.zh: 我不管你是医生还是护士。

sentences.en: It's a crime, in my opinion.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，这是犯罪。

sentences.en: And, you know, as a result, there were a lot of older people in New York who were really frustrated, really ruminating and anxious about when the vaccine was going to be available
sentences.zh: 结果，纽约有很多老年人感到非常沮丧，一直在反复思考和焦虑疫苗何时才能提供

sentences.en: to them.
sentences.zh: 给他们。

sentences.en: OK, so what is the situation in Florida, by contrast?
sentences.zh: 好的，那么相比之下，佛罗里达州的情况如何？

sentences.en: In Florida, Governor DeSantis decided he was going to do things a little differently.
sentences.zh: 在佛罗里达州，德桑蒂斯州长决定采取不同的做法。

sentences.en: Certainly, he is prioritizing health care workers and nursing home residents, but he's also putting in that immediate first group senior citizens.
sentences.zh: 当然，他优先考虑医护人员和养老院居民，但他同时也把老年人纳入了第一批接种群体。

sentences.en: Everybody over the age of 65 is now in the group that's allowed to get a vaccine as soon as it's available to them.
sentences.zh: 现在，所有65岁以上的人都在一旦有疫苗供应即可接种的群体中。

sentences.en: Huh.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And what is Governor DeSantis' explanation, his rationale for breaking with the CDC guidelines?
sentences.zh: 那么德桑蒂斯州长对于打破疾控中心指导方针的解释和理由是什么？

sentences.en: Well, good morning.
sentences.zh: 嗯，早上好。

sentences.en: It's great to be in Palm Beach County.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到棕榈滩县。

sentences.en: I want to thank the county mayor.
sentences.zh: 我要感谢县长。

sentences.en: So Governor DeSantis has talked about this a bit.
sentences.zh: 德桑蒂斯州长对此谈过一些。

sentences.en: You have people who fought in World War II, survived the HolocauSt.
sentences.zh: 你有经历过二战、在大屠杀中幸存下来的人。

sentences.en: And said just how important it is to reach the people who he calls the greatest generation.
sentences.zh: 他说，接触到他所称的“最伟大的一代”是多么重要。

sentences.en: And we have a responsibility to stand by those folks who've done so much to make our state and country what it is today.
sentences.zh: 我们有责任支持那些为我们的州和国家做出如此多贡献的人们。

sentences.en: And this is also his political base.
sentences.zh: 这也是他的政治基础。

sentences.en: Lots of people over 65 are Republicans in Florida.
sentences.zh: 在佛罗里达州，许多65岁以上的人都是共和党人。

sentences.en: So that's a factor, but it's not the only factor.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个因素，但不是唯一的因素。

sentences.en: And how are Floridians responding to DeSantis' approach here?
sentences.zh: 佛罗里达人对德桑蒂斯的这种做法有何反应？

sentences.en: Well, there's huge, huge demand in Florida, as you might imagine, with the huge senior citizen population down there.
sentences.zh: 嗯，正如你所想象的那样，佛罗里达州有着庞大的老年人口，需求非常非常大。

sentences.en: And it's a big mess.
sentences.zh: 而且情况一团糟。

sentences.en: Some people have heard about vaccination events and shown up and waited in huge long lines, even overnight, hoping they'll get a vaccine.
sentences.zh: 有些人听说有疫苗接种活动，就赶去排起长队，甚至通宵排队，希望能打上疫苗。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: Sometimes succeeding, sometimes not.
sentences.zh: 有时成功了，有时没有。

sentences.en: Others have, you know, spent hours, a whole day online trying to score an appointment through these very new registration sites for vaccination events.
sentences.zh: 其他人则在网上花了几个小时甚至一整天，试图通过这些非常新的疫苗接种登记网站预约。

sentences.en: Again, some succeed, many do not.
sentences.zh: 同样，有些人成功了，很多人没有。

sentences.en: A lot of these sites are crashing from overuse in, you know, just the first few hours.
sentences.zh: 许多网站因为使用过度，在最初的几个小时内就崩溃了。

sentences.en: So no matter how persistent and eager you are, there's still a good chance you're not going to get an appointment or a vaccination just yet.
sentences.zh: 所以无论你多么坚持和渴望，你仍然很有可能暂时无法获得预约或接种疫苗。

sentences.en: And that's super frustrating to people down there.
sentences.zh: 这对当地人来说非常令人沮丧。

sentences.en: So clearly we have a very significant division here in strategy, strict adherence to the CDC
sentences.zh: 显然，我们在策略上存在非常显著的分歧，纽约州严格遵守疾控中心

sentences.en: guidelines in New York, and a much looser, or I guess you could call it flexible, approach in Florida.
sentences.zh: 指导方针，而佛罗里达州则采取了更宽松，或者你可以称之为灵活的方法。

sentences.en: And since we are talking here about the sluggish pace of the vaccine rollout in the United States, which is working better?
sentences.zh: 既然我们在这里讨论美国疫苗推广缓慢的问题，哪种方式效果更好？

sentences.en: Which is seeming more efficient?
sentences.zh: 哪种方式看起来更有效率？

sentences.en: Well, if you look at the data, and we know that the data lags and is not entirely accurate,
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果你看数据，我们知道数据有滞后性，并不完全准确，

sentences.en: but the data we have now from the CDC says these two states are basically tied in the amount of vaccine they have administered, the number of shots they've gotten into arms so far.
sentences.zh: 但我们目前从疾控中心获得的数据显示，这两个州在疫苗接种量上基本持平，即到目前为止他们已经完成的注射次数。

sentences.en: And are either state's numbers considered impressive in the grand scheme of the 50 states or not?
sentences.zh: 那么在全美50个州的大局中，这两个州的数字被认为是令人印象深刻的吗？

sentences.en: You know what?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？

sentences.en: I'm really cautious to say what's impressive and not at this point, given the extremely limited data we have, and we're still in such early days.
sentences.zh: 鉴于我们拥有的数据极其有限，而且我们还处于早期阶段，我真的对评价什么是令人印象深刻持谨慎态度。

sentences.en: But just after the holidays, neither Florida nor New York were doing an especially great job of giving out the doses they had.
sentences.zh: 但在假期刚过时，佛罗里达州和纽约州在分发现有剂量方面做得都不算特别好。

sentences.en: But what's interesting is last week, the Trump administration came out and started to suggest the Florida way was the way to go, and that everyone else should follow their lead.
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是，上周特朗普政府开始暗示佛罗里达的方式才是正道，其他人应该效仿。

sentences.en: We have U.S.
sentences.zh: 我们有美国

sentences.en: Surgeon General Dr. Jerome AdaMs. He joins us now this morning.
sentences.zh: 卫生局局长杰罗姆·亚当斯博士。他现在加入了我们的早间节目。

sentences.en: Dr. Adams, thank you for talking with us this morning.
sentences.zh: 亚当斯博士，感谢您今早与我们交谈。

sentences.en: We heard Jerome Adams, the Surgeon General, come out and say, you know what?
sentences.zh: 我们听到卫生局局长杰罗姆·亚当斯出来说，你知道吗？

sentences.en: If the demand isn't there in 1A, go to 1B and continue on down.
sentences.zh: 如果1A类人群需求不足，就转向1B类，以此类推。

sentences.en: And if the demand isn't there in one location, move those vaccines to another location.
sentences.zh: 如果一个地方需求不足，就把疫苗转移到另一个地方。

sentences.en: Go to the next priority group and continue on down the line to the next and the next.
sentences.zh: 去下一个优先群体，然后继续排队到下一个，再下一个。

sentences.en: So your headline today really should be, Surgeon General tells states and governors to move quickly to other priority groups.
sentences.zh: 所以你今天的头条新闻应该是，卫生局局长告诉各州和州长迅速转向其他优先群体。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So how do you explain that?
sentences.zh: 那么你如何解释这一点？

sentences.en: Because from what you just said, letting people jump the line, violating the CDC guidelines, that was not speeding things up.

sentences.en: And there's just so much pent up demand for this vaccine, so much anxiety and angst and anger about wanting it now that the administration's really feeling

sentences.en: some pressure about that.

sentences.en: It was partly due to news coming out that at least some clinics were ending up throwing
sentences.zh: 这部分是因为有消息传出，至少有一些诊所最终不得不扔掉

sentences.en: And that's just about everyone's nightmare in this moment, vaccines being tossed out and not used.

sentences.en: Right.

sentences.en: Once the vials are open, there's only a pretty finite amount of time you can keep them around before you have to throw them away.

sentences.en: So despite these original guidelines, which a lot of experts saw as important and worth adhering to,

sentences.en: But it's going to push more vaccine into the system more quickly.
sentences.zh: 但这将使更多的疫苗更快地进入系统。

sentences.en: But what Biden is proposing, wouldn't that potentially just overburden an inefficient system that is, as you have described here, already struggling to administer the doses it has?

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对会。

sentences.en: That's a huge risk, just from what we're seeing in a place like Florida so far, which cannot begin to keep up with the enormous demand.

sentences.en: And, you know, it's just begun.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这仅仅是个开始。

sentences.en: The fine tuning is in process.

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。
